statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), len(r) = 2, and exactly one of the following holds: (a) r[0] = -1, r[1] = -1, and for every i and j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, it is not the case that both |i - j| >= indexDifference and |nums[i] - nums[j]| >= valueDifference; (b) 0 <= r[0] < n, 0 <= r[1] < n, |r[0] - r[1]| >= indexDifference, and |nums[r[0]] - nums[r[1]]| >= valueDifference.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000; 0 <= indexDifference <= 100000; 0 <= valueDifference <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular, for every input satisfying the preconditions it does not fail (no panic, overflow, or out-of-bounds).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000; 0 <= indexDifference <= 100000; 0 <= valueDifference <= 1000000000.

preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000; 0 <= indexDifference <= 100000; 0 <= valueDifference <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with len(r) = 2, for each k in {0,1}, either r[k] = -1 or 0 <= r[k] < n; moreover, r[0] = -1 if and only if r[1] = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000; 0 <= indexDifference <= 100000; 0 <= valueDifference <= 1000000000.

preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, 0 <= nums[k] <= 1000000000; 0 <= indexDifference <= 100000; 0 <= valueDifference <= 1000000000.
